summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the theme of brotherhood in Parashat Vayishlah by examining the seven-fold repetition of the word 'brother' in the narrative of Yaakov and Esav. She uses the seven days of creation as a structural framework to analyze how different aspects of sibling relationships, such as unity, boundaries, and reconciliation, can be understood and applied to our own lives.
questions: How can we reconcile with family members after a long period of conflict?
Why does the Torah emphasize the word 'brother' seven times in the stories of Kayin and Hevel and Yaakov and Esav?
How can we maintain our own identity while still being part of a unified family?
What can the seven days of creation teach us about building peace in our relationships?
Is it possible to forgive someone who we feel has wronged us?
